why: Removing C4 removed a protection against cutting at noun-phrase / name-internal boundaries, so the scorer began placing earlier cuts inside multiword NPs/named entities (examples: 'John ‖ Nixon', 'Cirque ‖ du Soleil', 'We ‖ will ‖ never...'). That change raised agreement at rank‑1 but worsened ranks 2–3 (rank_depth: +0.124 at depth1, −0.216/−0.098 at depths2–3), produced mixed counts (n_better 2287 vs n_worse 1926), and caused a measurable drop in the mid‑length bin (≤10: −0.0044).
lesson: If you remove a rule that overlaps clausal-attachment checks, keep an explicit constraint (or reweighting) that prevents cuts inside multiword names/NP-internal boundaries so top choice gains don’t come at the expense of deeper-ranked cuts used by shorter-latency budgets.
